avatar_uri.description: The URI of the agent's avatar. Avatars are used throughout the Dialogflow console and in the self-hosted Web Demo integration.
avatar_uri.rationale: Controls the cosmetic avatar URI shown in Dialogflow interfaces; constraining branding references does not improve the agent's security.

default_language_code.description:
The default language of the agent as a language tag. [See Language Support](https://cloud.google.com/dialogflow/cx/docs/reference/language)
for a list of the currently supported language codes. This field cannot be updated after creation.
default_language_code.rationale: Selects the agent's primary language, which is a functional product choice with no universally more secure value.

delete_chat_engine_on_destroy.description:
If set to 'true', Terraform will delete the chat engine associated with the agent when the agent is destroyed.
Otherwise, the chat engine will persist.

This virtual field addresses a critical dependency chain: 'agent' -> 'engine' -> 'data store'. The chat engine is automatically
provisioned when a data store is linked to the agent, meaning Terraform doesn't have direct control over its lifecycle as a managed
resource. This creates a problem when both the agent and data store are managed by Terraform and need to be destroyed. Without
delete_chat_engine_on_destroy set to true, the data store's deletion would fail because the unmanaged chat engine would still be
using it. This setting ensures that the entire dependency chain can be properly torn down.
See 'mmv1/templates/terraform/examples/dialogflowcx_tool_data_store.tf.tmpl' as an example.

Data store can be linked to an agent through the 'knowledgeConnectorSettings' field of a [flow](https://cloud.google.com/dialogflow/cx/docs/reference/rest/v3/projects.locations.agents.flows#resource:-flow)
or a [page](https://cloud.google.com/dialogflow/cx/docs/reference/rest/v3/projects.locations.agents.flows.pages#resource:-page)
or the 'dataStoreSpec' field of a [tool](https://cloud.google.com/dialogflow/cx/docs/reference/rest/v3/projects.locations.agents.tools#resource:-tool).
The ID of the implicitly created engine is stored in the 'genAppBuilderSettings' field of the [agent](https://cloud.google.com/dialogflow/cx/docs/reference/rest/v3/projects.locations.agents#resource:-agent).
delete_chat_engine_on_destroy.rationale: Controls lifecycle cleanup of an implicitly created chat engine so linked data stores can be deleted; this is an operational dependency choice rather than a generic security control.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Controls whether Terraform can destroy the agent. Requiring PREVENT blocks accidental deletion and resulting loss of the agent configuration.

description.description: The description of this agent. The maximum length is 500 characters. If exceeded, the request is rejected.
description.rationale: Provides a human-readable description and does not configure a security boundary or control.

display_name.description: The human-readable name of the agent, unique within the location.
display_name.rationale: Names the agent within its location; naming conventions are organisation-specific and are not a generic security control.

enable_multi_language_training.description: Enable training multi-lingual models for this agent. These models will be trained on all the languages supported by the agent.
enable_multi_language_training.rationale: Enables training across supported languages, which is a product capability choice rather than a platform-level security setting.

enable_spell_correction.description: Indicates if automatic spell correction is enabled in detect intent requests.
enable_spell_correction.rationale: Controls automatic spelling correction for requests; it changes conversational behaviour but does not provide a generic security guarantee.

enable_stackdriver_logging.description: Determines whether this agent should log conversation queries.
enable_stackdriver_logging.rationale: Controls whether Dialogflow CX logs conversation queries. Requiring it to be true preserves audit visibility and diagnostic telemetry, even though newer configuration exposes the same capability.

location.description:
The name of the location this agent is located in.

~> **Note:** The first time you are deploying an Agent in your project you must configure location settings.
 This is a one time step but at the moment you can only [configure location settings](https://cloud.google.com/dialogflow/cx/docs/concept/region#location-settings) via the Dialogflow CX console.
 Another options is to use global location so you don't need to manually configure location settings.
location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

locked.description: Indicates whether the agent is locked for changes. If the agent is locked, modifications to the agent will be rejected except for [agents.restore][].
locked.rationale: Prevents changes to an approved agent configuration except restoration. Requiring the lock reduces unauthorised or accidental configuration changes.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Identifies the project that owns the resource; platform policy must not prescribe team-specific project references.

security_settings.description: Name of the SecuritySettings reference for the agent. Format: projects/<Project ID>/locations/<Location ID>/securitySettings/<Security Settings ID>.
security_settings.rationale: References a separate Dialogflow CX SecuritySettings resource. This policy should secure that resource's configuration rather than dictate which team-specific reference an agent uses.

start_playbook.description: Name of the start playbook in this agent. A start playbook will be automatically created when the agent is created, and can only be deleted by deleting the agent. Format: **projects/<ProjectID>/locations/<LocationID>/agents/<AgentID>/playbooks/<PlaybookID>**. Currently only the default playbook with id "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000" is allowed.
start_playbook.rationale: References the agent's start playbook; selecting a playbook is application behaviour and not a generic security constraint.

supported_language_codes.description: The list of all languages supported by this agent (except for the default_language_code).
supported_language_codes.rationale: Lists supported languages, a functional localisation choice with no universally secure allowlist.

time_zone.description:
The time zone of this agent from the [time zone database](https://www.iana.org/time-zones), e.g., America/New_York,
Europe/Paris.
time_zone.rationale: Sets the agent's business time zone and does not control access, encryption, logging, or data residency.

advanced_settings.description:
Hierarchical advanced settings for this agent. The settings exposed at the lower level overrides the settings exposed at the higher level.
Hierarchy: Agent->Flow->Page->Fulfillment/Parameter.

advanced_settings.audio_export_gcs_desti.description:
If present, incoming audio is exported by Dialogflow to the configured Google Cloud Storage destination. Exposed at the following levels:
* Agent level
* Flow level

The Google Cloud Storage URI for the exported objects. Whether a full object name, or just a prefix, its usage depends on the Dialogflow operation.
Format: gs://bucket/object-name-or-prefix
advanced_settings.audio_export_gcs_desti.rationale: Points audio exports to a Cloud Storage path. The bucket itself must be secured; constraining this team-specific destination reference would overreach.

advanced_settings.dtmf_settings.description:
Define behaviors for DTMF (dual tone multi frequency). DTMF settings does not override each other. DTMF settings set at different levels define DTMF detections running in parallel. Exposed at the following levels:
* Agent level
* Flow level
* Page level
* Parameter level

advanced_settings.dtmf_settings.enabled.description: If true, incoming audio is processed for DTMF (dual tone multi frequency) events. For example, if the caller presses a button on their telephone keypad and DTMF processing is enabled, Dialogflow will detect the event (e.g. a "3" was pressed) in the incoming audio and pass the event to the bot to drive business logic (e.g. when 3 is pressed, return the account balance).
advanced_settings.dtmf_settings.enabled.rationale: Enables DTMF event processing for conversational flows, which is a functional telephony setting rather than a platform security control.

advanced_settings.dtmf_settings.finish_d.description: The digit that terminates a DTMF digit sequence.
advanced_settings.dtmf_settings.finish_d.rationale: Selects the digit that ends a DTMF sequence; this is application interaction behaviour with no generic secure value.

advanced_settings.dtmf_settings.max_digi.rationale: Sets the maximum DTMF sequence length, an application input design choice that is not a generic infrastructure security control.

advanced_settings.logging_settings.description:
Settings for logging. Settings for Dialogflow History, Contact Center messages, StackDriver logs, and speech logging. Exposed at the following levels:
* Agent level

advanced_settings.logging_settings.enabl.description: Enables consent-based end-user input redaction, if true, a pre-defined session parameter **$session.params.conversation-redaction** will be used to determine if the utterance should be redacted.
advanced_settings.logging_settings.enabl.rationale: Enables session-driven redaction of end-user utterances when an agent is configured to collect consent and handle data that requires redaction. Because this is an application-specific privacy feature and agents may legitimately have no such data or consent workflow, enabling it is not a universal security baseline for every Dialogflow CX agent.

Enables collection and storage of end-user conversation history for product features and quality improvement. Requiring it globally can increase data retention, so it is not a universally safer configuration.
Enables Google Cloud Logging for the agent. Requiring it ensures activity is available for monitoring and incident investigation.

advanced_settings.speech_settings.description:
Settings for speech to text detection. Exposed at the following levels:
* Agent level
* Flow level
* Page level
* Parameter level

advanced_settings.speech_settings.endpoi.description: Sensitivity of the speech model that detects the end of speech. Scale from 0 to 100.
advanced_settings.speech_settings.endpoi.rationale: Tunes speech end-of-utterance detection sensitivity, which affects recognition behaviour but not a generic security boundary.

advanced_settings.speech_settings.models.description:
Mapping from language to Speech-to-Text model. The mapped Speech-to-Text model will be selected for requests from its corresponding language. For more information, see [Speech models](https://cloud.google.com/dialogflow/cx/docs/concept/speech-models).
An object containing a list of **"key": value** pairs. Example: **{ "name": "wrench", "mass": "1.3kg", "count": "3" }**.
advanced_settings.speech_settings.models.rationale: Maps languages to speech-recognition models; model selection is a functional quality choice with no universal secure value.

advanced_settings.speech_settings.no_spe.description:
Timeout before detecting no speech.
A duration in seconds with up to nine fractional digits, ending with 's'. Example: "3.5s".
advanced_settings.speech_settings.no_spe.rationale: Sets a speech timeout for conversation flow handling and does not secure the resource or its data.

advanced_settings.speech_settings.use_ti.description: Use timeout based endpointing, interpreting endpointer sensitivity as seconds of timeout value.
advanced_settings.speech_settings.use_ti.rationale: Changes the endpointing algorithm for speech detection, a functional configuration with no generic security direction.

answer_feedback_settings.enable_answer_f.description:
If enabled, end users will be able to provide [answer feedback](https://cloud.google.com/dialogflow/cx/docs/reference/rest/v3/projects.locations.agents.sessions/submitAnswerFeedback#body.AnswerFeedback)
to Dialogflow responses. Feature works only if interaction logging is enabled in the Dialogflow agent.
answer_feedback_settings.enable_answer_f.rationale: Allows end users to submit answer feedback. Whether to collect this product feedback requires application-specific privacy decisions, not a universal policy.

client_certificate_settings.passphrase.description: The name of the SecretManager secret version resource storing the passphrase. 'passphrase' should be left unset if the private key is not encrypted. Format: **projects/{project}/secrets/{secret}/versions/{version}**
client_certificate_settings.passphrase.rationale: References a Secret Manager version that stores a private-key passphrase. The provider already requires a secret reference, and policy must not pin team-specific secret paths.

client_certificate_settings.private_key.description: The name of the SecretManager secret version resource storing the private key encoded in PEM format. Format: **projects/{project}/secrets/{secret}/versions/{version}**
client_certificate_settings.private_key.rationale: References a Secret Manager version containing the private key. It is a reference to another secured resource, so a generic policy should not constrain its specific path.

client_certificate_settings.ssl_certific.description: The ssl certificate encoded in PEM format. This string must include the begin header and end footer lines.
client_certificate_settings.ssl_certific.rationale: Contains PEM certificate content. The certificate's identity and lifecycle are organisation-specific, so the free-form value cannot be meaningfully constrained by a generic policy.

gen_app_builder_settings.engine.description:
The full name of the Gen App Builder engine related to this agent if there is one.
Format: projects/{Project ID}/locations/{Location ID}/collections/{Collection ID}/engines/{Engine ID}
gen_app_builder_settings.engine.rationale: References a Gen App Builder engine. This contribution secures the agent rather than prescribing which external engine a team may use.

git_integration_settings.description: Git integration settings for this agent.

git_integration_settings.github_settings.description: The access token used to authenticate the access to the GitHub repository.
git_integration_settings.github_settings.rationale: Supplies an opaque GitHub credential. A generic policy cannot safely inspect or approve its secret value; credential storage and rotation are handled outside this field.

git_integration_settings.github_settings.description: A list of branches configured to be used from Dialogflow.
git_integration_settings.github_settings.rationale: Lists GitHub branches for integration, which is a team workflow choice with no universal secure branch set.

git_integration_settings.github_settings.description: The unique repository display name for the GitHub repository.
git_integration_settings.github_settings.rationale: Provides a display name for the linked repository and has no security effect.

git_integration_settings.github_settings.description: The GitHub repository URI related to the agent.
git_integration_settings.github_settings.rationale: References a team-specific GitHub repository. Platform policy should not prescribe external repository references.

git_integration_settings.github_settings.description: The branch of the GitHub repository tracked for this agent.
git_integration_settings.github_settings.rationale: Selects the branch tracked by the Git integration; this is a deployment workflow decision rather than a generic security control.

personalization_settings.default_end_use.description:
Default end user metadata, used when processing DetectIntent requests. Recommended to be filled as a template instead of hard-coded value, for example { "age": "$session.params.age" }.
The data will be merged with the [QueryParameters.end_user_metadata](https://cloud.google.com/dialogflow/cx/docs/reference/rest/v3/QueryParameters#FIELDS.end_user_metadata)
in [DetectIntentRequest.query_params](https://cloud.google.com/dialogflow/cx/docs/reference/rest/v3/projects.locations.agents.sessions/detectIntent#body.request_body.FIELDS.query_params) during query processing.

This field uses JSON data as a string. The value provided must be a valid JSON representation documented in [Struct](https://protobuf.dev/reference/protobuf/google.protobuf/#struct).
personalization_settings.default_end_use.rationale: Contains free-form end-user metadata JSON. Its permitted fields require application-specific data governance and cannot be safely constrained by a generic policy.

speech_to_text_settings.enable_speech_ad.description: Whether to use speech adaptation for speech recognition.
speech_to_text_settings.enable_speech_ad.rationale: Enables a speech-recognition quality feature and does not establish a security control or data boundary.

text_to_speech_settings.synthesize_speec.description:
Configuration of how speech should be synthesized, mapping from [language](https://cloud.google.com/dialogflow/cx/docs/reference/language) to [SynthesizeSpeechConfig](https://cloud.google.com/dialogflow/cx/docs/reference/rest/v3/projects.locations.agents#synthesizespeechconfig).
These settings affect:
* The phone gateway synthesize configuration set via Agent.text_to_speech_settings.
* How speech is synthesized when invoking session APIs. 'Agent.text_to_speech_settings' only applies if 'OutputAudioConfig.synthesize_speech_config' is not specified.
text_to_speech_settings.synthesize_speec.rationale: Contains free-form speech-synthesis configuration, which affects output behaviour but has no generic security constraint.
